content: Firestore offline writes vs rules (official docs + SDK behavior): local writes apply immediately and sync later (last-write-wins per doc). Security rules are NOT evaluated offline — a write queued while offline that violates rules succeeds locally and fails on sync; the write promise rejects with permission-denied and the local doc reverts to server state (community-reported edge cases of stuck pending writes on the JS SDK exist in firebase-js-sdk issue tracker — MEDIUM confidence). Detection: snapshot.metadata.hasPendingWrites stays true while unsynced; waitForPendingWrites() resolves when all writes are acknowledged; includeMetadataChanges in onSnapshot is needed to observe hasPendingWrites/fromCache transitions. A write that will never succeed (rules violation) can leave the UI showing data that will be reverted — apps must catch write-promise rejections and surface them.
